properties.statement:
A FIX THAT NEVER CLOSED ITS FINDING MISLED THE NEXT FIXER. 2026-09-06: a feedback ledger computed from the graph (a defect fact is 'open' unless a ChangeEvent INVALIDATES it) listed fact:defect-unsatisfied-requirement-fires-on-requirements-whose-status-is-the-answer as open. It was not: chg:the-surface-says-what-it-already-knew had built the reporter's own alternative (a deferred requirement is asked a different, lower-ranked 'still parked?' question) and pinned it in the_surface_says_what_it_already_knew.rs — but drew no INVALIDATES edge. Trusting the recorded fact instead of searching precedent (root-cause step ②), the session made `unsatisfied_requirement` skip `deferred` outright. That silenced the designed question. Two existing pins failed within the hour; the change was reverted and the fact closed from its real fixer.

WHAT THIS IS AN INSTANCE OF: a record that is true when written and silently overtaken — the same class as fact:defect-a-status-can-advance-past-its-own-prose-and-nothing-says-so, on the fix axis instead of the status axis. req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause is ACCEPTED and asks that a repair record what it reached; this is the case where the repair recorded nothing about the finding at all.

THE OWNER'S QUESTION THAT CAUGHT IT: Anthony asked mid-build 'we have done /root-cause on all the issues we're fixing? I don't want to fix a symptom or the wrong thing.' The honest answer was: two of four fully; this one had a confirmed mechanism but no precedent search. The precedent search is what would have found the existing pins BEFORE the code.

THE THIRD LEG THIS NAMES: nothing detects 'a defect fact whose subject artifact has a later accepted change and no INVALIDATES from any ChangeEvent'. That detector would have flagged this fact on the day the fix landed. Not built; recorded as owed alongside the feedback-triage rule's own missing detector.

BOUNDS: one instance, found by the test suite rather than by the record; how many other open-looking defect facts are already fixed is not measured — the ledger's other 'open' rows deserve the same suspicion.
